title: Choosing generators of a regular prime with controlled annihilators (Ogoma)
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subset\Lambda$ an ideal and $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal with $I\subset\mathfrak q$, and let $n,e\ge1$ be integers. Assume $\mathfrak q^n\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\subset I\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$, where $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is the localization at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and that $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $d$. Then there are $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d\in\Lambda$ such that (1) the images of $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$ generate $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$; (2) $\pi_1^n,\dots,\pi_d^n\in I$; (3) for $i=1,\dots,d$, writing $M_i=\Lambda/(\pi_1^e,\dots,\pi_{i-1}^e)\Lambda$, one has $\{m\in M_i:\pi_im=0\}=\{m\in M_i:\pi_i^2m=0\}$, i.e. $\mathrm{Ann}_{M_i}(\pi_i)=\mathrm{Ann}_{M_i}(\pi_i^2)$. (Stacks writes 'there exists an $n>0$ and $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_d$'; the $n$ is the given one.)
